ideas.title: Parameter-efficient adaptation of vision transformers for small image datasets
ideas.description: Adapt a pretrained vision transformer to small image-classification datasets using low-rank adapters and lightweight regularization, targeting accuracy close to full fine-tuning with substantially fewer trainable parameters.
ideas.research_question: Can low-rank adapters with lightweight regularization match full fine-tuning on small image-classification datasets while reducing trainable parameters and memory?
atomic_claims: Low-rank adaptation can approach full fine-tuning accuracy with fewer trainable parameters.
Adapter rank and regularization strength have measurable low-data accuracy and calibration trade-offs.
The method should be compared with linear probing, full fine-tuning, visual prompt tuning, and standard adapters on fixed data splits.
success_criteria: Report accuracy, macro F1, calibration error, trainable parameters, peak memory, and training time.
Use at least two small public image-classification datasets and three random seeds.
Include rank, regularization, and data-fraction ablations without changing test splits.
subproblems: Which parameter-efficient adaptation components and training objectives are reproducible baselines for pretrained vision transformers?
Which datasets, low-data splits, metrics, and competing baselines are used to evaluate parameter-efficient vision adaptation?
What accuracy, calibration, memory, and compute trade-offs or limitations are reported?

ideas.title: Masked self-supervised pretraining for time-series classification
ideas.description: Study whether simple masked reconstruction pretraining improves time-series classification when labeled samples are limited.
ideas.research_question: When labels are limited, does masked reconstruction pretraining improve time-series classification over supervised training from scratch?
atomic_claims: Mask ratio and pretraining data diversity affect transfer quality.
success_criteria: Evaluate fixed label fractions and multiple seeds.
Compare with training from scratch and contrastive pretraining.
subproblems: Which masking and reconstruction objectives are reproducible?
Which datasets and label-fraction protocols are standard?
Which baselines and ablations are required?

ideas.title: Sparse graph regularization for interpretable multivariate time-series anomaly detection
ideas.description: Add a sparse learned dependency graph to a standard multivariate anomaly detector and evaluate detection plus variable-level explanations.
ideas.research_question: Can sparse graph regularization improve variable-level explanations without reducing multivariate anomaly-detection accuracy?
atomic_claims: Sparse dependencies can identify variables related to an anomaly.
Graph sparsity creates a measurable accuracy-interpretability trade-off.
success_criteria: Report F1 and AUROC with explanation fidelity and sparsity.
Compare with a non-graph detector and a dense graph variant.
subproblems: Which graph anomaly detectors are reproducible baselines?
Which public datasets and leakage controls are standard?

ideas.title: Relation-aware negative sampling for knowledge-graph link prediction
ideas.description: Use relation type constraints to sample harder but valid negatives for a standard knowledge-graph embedding model.
ideas.research_question: Does relation-aware negative sampling improve link prediction over uniform corruption at similar training cost?
atomic_claims: Harder negatives improve filtered ranking metrics when false-negative risk is controlled.
success_criteria: Compare uniform, frequency-based, self-adversarial, and relation-aware sampling.
subproblems: Which negative-sampling methods are strong baselines?
Which datasets and filtered metrics are standard?

ideas.title: Lightweight calibrated uncertainty for multivariate time-series forecasting
ideas.description: Add a lightweight conformal calibration layer to a compact forecasting model and evaluate interval coverage under distribution shift.
ideas.research_question: Can a lightweight conformal layer provide calibrated forecast intervals under moderate temporal shift without retraining the forecaster?
atomic_claims: Post-hoc calibration can improve interval coverage.
Rolling calibration adapts to moderate temporal shift.
success_criteria: Report coverage, interval width, MAE, and calibration runtime.
Separate calibration and test windows chronologically.
subproblems: How are coverage and interval efficiency reported?
